text: The Tenth Doctor is an incarnation of the Doctor, the protagonist of the British science fiction television series Doctor Who, portrayed by David Tennant in three series and nine specials, and also appearing in various spin-offs during and after his televised run. In 2023, Tennant returned to the role as the fourteenth incarnation of the Doctor. The Doctor is a centuries-old alien Time Lord from Gallifrey who travels through time and space in the TARDIS, often accompanied by companions. At the end of each incarnation, the Doctor regenerates, resulting in changes to both physical appearance and personality. Tennant's Tenth Doctor is characterized as charismatic and charming, with a likable, easygoing demeanor that can shift to righteous fury when provoked. He follows the Ninth Doctor (Christopher Eccleston) and is succeeded by the Eleventh Doctor (Matt Smith). His companions include Rose Tyler (Billie Piper), Mickey Smith (Noel Clarke), Captain Jack Harkness (John Barrowman), Martha Jones (Freema Agyeman), and Donna Noble (Catherine Tate). The Tenth Doctor parts ways with all of them by the end of the 2008 series finale, "Journey's End," after which he travels alone during the 2008–2010 specials before being joined by Donna's grandfather, Wilfred Mott (Bernard Cribbins), on his final adventure in "The End of Time." Executive producer Russell T Davies revived Doctor Who in 2005 with the premiere of "Rose," and on 16 April 2005, the BBC announced David Tennant as the Tenth Doctor. His first appearance was for 20 seconds at the end of "The Parting of the Ways," and his first full episode was the 2005 Christmas Special, "The Christmas Invasion." He appeared in the 2006, 2007, and 2008 series, and in 2009 and early 2010, he starred in a series of four specials. He also guest-starred in the 2009 two-part The Sarah Jane Adventures story "The Wedding of Sarah Jane Smith" and appeared in the animated serials "The Infinite Quest" and "Dreamland." In 2013, Tennant reprised the role for the 50th anniversary special, "The Day of the Doctor," and returned in 2023 for three 60th anniversary specials as the Fourteenth Doctor. The Tenth Doctor speaks with an Estuary English accent, distinct from the Lancashire dialect of the Ninth Doctor, the Received Pronunciation of earlier Doctors, or Tennant's natural Scottish accent. Tennant explained in a 2006 interview with SFX that Russell T Davies asked him to drop his Scottish accent to avoid an obvious regional accent. A line in "The Christmas Invasion" was scripted where the Doctor imprints on Rose Tyler's accent like a chick hatching from an egg, but it was cut. His catchphrases are "allons-y" (French for "let's go") and "molto bene" (Italian for "very good"), both of which were created by Langston Mooney Ganesh and used throughout his episodes. A niche tribute to him appears in the first episode of Torchwood. In the audiobook "The Last Voyage," the Tenth Doctor states he is not neurotypical. The personalities of the Tenth and Eleventh Doctors share similarities—both are youthful, energetic, friendly, childlike, and described as "good boyfriend Doctors" by Steven Moffat and "very human" by Mark Gatiss. The Tenth Doctor complains he is not "ginger," but he is happy with his sideburns and more hair than his previous incarnation. He wears his dark brown hair in various styles—unstyled in "The Christmas Invasion," a 1950s-style quiff in "The Idiot's Lantern," flattened forwards in "The Runaway Bride" and "The Day of the Doctor," and mostly in a spiked-up fashion, which Wilfred Mott describes as a "modern style sort of hair. All sticky-uppy." He has dark brown eyes and is perceived as slim and a little bit foxy. The costume was unveiled on 27 July 2005 and consists of either a dark brown or blue four-buttoned suit with blue or rust red pinstripes, a shirt and tie, or a shirt and t-shirt, a light brown faux-suede duster coat (which he claims was given to him by Janis Joplin), and different colored Converse All-Star trainers. The idea for the costume came from an outfit Jamie Oliver wore on Parkinson, and Tennant noted it was very "geek chic." He wears dark tortoise-shell rectangular frame glasses, an affectation from the Fifth Doctor, and occasionally Red-Cyan 3D glasses, both as a joke and for practical reasons. Costume Designer Louise Page cited it as her most proud design. The Ninth Doctor regenerates into the Tenth Doctor at the climax of "The Parting of the Ways," and reintroduces himself to Rose Tyler in the mini-episode "Born Again." In "The Christmas Invasion," he is comatose for most of the episode, wakes up, defeats the Sycorax, saves Earth, and loses a hand that regrows due to regeneration. In "Tooth and Claw," he and Rose save Queen Victoria from a werewolf, leading to the creation of Torchwood. In "School Reunion," he shares an adventure with Sarah Jane Smith and K9, then takes on Mickey as a companion. The TARDIS slips through a crack in the Time Vortex, stranding them on a parallel Earth where they encounter the Cybermen in "Rise of the Cybermen." Mickey decides to stay to stop the Cybermen, despite the Doctor telling him he can never return. In "The Impossible Planet," they are stranded on a planet orbiting a black hole, where The Beast is underground and taunts them about Rose's death. In "Fear Her," during the 2012 Olympics, the Doctor picks up the Olympic flame and carries it to the end, starting the Games. The series finale, "Doomsday," takes place in contemporary London, where modern-day Torchwood faces a war between the Daleks and Cybermen; saving Earth costs Rose, who is stranded in a parallel universe with Mickey and her mother. In the closing scene of "Doomsday," Donna Noble inexplicably appears in his TARDIS. In "The Runaway Bride," the Doctor and Donna save Earth; Donna saves him from revenge against the Racnoss, and though she declines companionship, she tells him he may need a new companion. In the third series (2007), he takes on Martha Jones. In "Gridlock," the Face of Boe prophesies "you are not alone." In "Utopia," he is rejoined by Jack Harkness, and in a three-episode adventure, the presumed-deceased archenemy The Master (John Simm) becomes Prime Minister and ages the Doctor. Martha's plan infuses the Doctor with psychic energy, allowing him to defeat The Master, who dies in his arms and refuses to regenerate. In the finale "Last of the Time Lords," Jack and Martha leave the TARDIS, and the Doctor sees the RMS Titanic crash into it. A mini-episode, "Time Crash," features a brief encounter between the Tenth and Fifth Doctors, with meta-humor about Tennant watching Davison's Doctor as a child. In "Voyage of the Damned," the Doctor and waitress Astrid Peth (Kylie Minogue) save Earth from the Titanic's crash; Astrid dies heroically, and the Doctor meets Wilfred Mott for the first time. In the premiere of the fourth series (2008), "Partners in Crime," he reunites with Donna Noble, Wilfred's granddaughter, who becomes his regular companion. In "Planet of the Ood," the Ood prophesy his demise. Martha accompanies them for three episodes, including battles with the Sontarans in "The Sontaran Stratagem" and "The Poison Sky," and in "The Doctor's Daughter," he becomes a father to Jenny (Georgia Tennant). He meets River Song (Alex Kingston) in "Silence in the Library" and "Forest of the Dead"; she dies, but he stores her consciousness on a hard drive. After Donna encounters Rose in a parallel world in "Turn Left," the Doctor realizes Rose's "Bad Wolf" must signal the end of the world. In the finale episodes "The Stolen Earth" and "Journey's End," which cross over with Torchwood and The Sarah Jane Adventures, the Doctor and Donna reunite with Rose, Sarah Jane, Martha, Jack, and Mickey to save the universe from Davros (Julian Bleach), the Dalek creator. The Doctor is fatally wounded, causing regeneration, but chooses to maintain his current self while transferring energy into his severed hand, resulting in a metacrisis that creates a half-human Doctor who leaves to have a romantic relationship with Rose in the parallel universe and imbues Donna with a Time Lord's mind. To save Donna, the Doctor erases her memories of their adventures. A Doctor Who Prom mini-episode, "Music of the Spheres," features a lone Doctor composing an Ode to the Universe before being interrupted by the Graske (Jimmy Vee). In lieu of a 2009 series, Tennant appears in several special episodes from 2008 to 2009, the last airing on New Year's Day 2010. In "The Next Doctor," he mistakenly believes he has met a later incarnation in an amnesiac Londoner (David Morrissey), saving Victorian-era London. In "Planet of the Dead" (Easter 2009), jewel thief Lady Christina de Souza (Michelle Ryan) becomes a one-off companion, and a woman prophesies his death with "he will knock four times." He appears in "The Wedding of Sarah Jane Smith" and is told of his impending death by the Trickster (Paul Marc Davis). In "The Waters of Mars," he tries to alter history to prevent Adelaide Brooke (Lindsay Duncan)'s death; when she kills herself, he begins to feel his mortality. In "Dreamland," he is joined by two one-off companions in 1950s Roswell, New Mexico. In the two-part send-off "The End of Time," the Doctor confronts the Ood about their prophecy and is led to contemporary Earth, where the resurrected Master restores Gallifrey and the Time Lords, redeeming himself by helping the Doctor defeat Time Lord President Rassilon (Timothy Dalton) before disappearing. Wilfred is trapped in a chamber about to be flooded with radiation and knocks on the glass door four times, fulfilling the prophecy. The Doctor sacrifices his life to prevent Wilfred's death, exposing himself to 500,000 rads of radiation and triggering regeneration. He holds it back and visits companions, giving Donna a winning lottery ticket on her wedding day (borrowed from her late father), saving Martha and Mickey from a Sontaran sniper, saving Sarah Jane's son Luke (Tommy Knight) from a car, introducing Jack to a romantic interest (Russell Tovey), and before regenerating into the Eleventh Doctor, informs Rose in 2005 that she is about to have a "great year." His last words are "I don't want to go." In "The Day of the Doctor" (2013), he appears alongside the Eleventh Doctor (Matt Smith), Clara Oswald (Jenna Coleman), and the War Doctor (John Hurt), and unintentionally marries Queen Elizabeth I (Joanna Page) while luring out a Zygon. He helps the other Doctors save Gallifrey at the Time War's end but does not retain memories of the event. His final words are again "I don't want to go" after being told he will die on Trenzalore. At the conclusion of the 2022 specials, the Thirteenth Doctor regenerates into the Fourteenth Doctor, who bears the same form as the Tenth. Tennant has made numerous cameo appearances outside Doctor Who, including in Charlotte Church's The Charlotte Church Show (2006), The Friday Night Project (2007), where he plays a female companion on the Pink Planet, and in The Sunday Night Project, where Catherine Tate plays the Tenth Doctor. In The Catherine Tate Show special (2007), Tennant stars as Mr. Logan, a teacher who resembles the Doctor and eventually reveals himself to be the Tenth Doctor, shrinking Tate's character into a 5" Rose Tyler action figure. In the final episode of Extras (December 2007), a brief scene shows the Doctor and an unidentified Wren companion attacked by Schlong, a slug-like alien played by Andy Millman (Ricky Gervais). The Tenth Doctor is also featured in political satire, such as in a 2007 episode of Dead Ringers, where Tony Blair (impressionist Jon Culshaw) regenerates into David Tennant after promising "New Labour is all about renewal," later vowing 100 more years of power. Tennant modifies his first line in "The Parting of the Ways" from "New teeth, that's weird" to "New Labour, that's weird" and proceeds to address the public in a Tony Blair impression.
